doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Roy's commercial production company and voiceovers
summary: Roy produces commercials for Cheerios, Plymouth and Borden's, working with storyboards and timing, and gets voiceover work.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: And we went back finally after months of traveling, we went back to New York and I started a production company just specifically to do television commercials. Now I had to attend a lot of meetings where they’re arguing over whether it should be AND or BUT in the copy. And it’s going back and forth.
Yeah. Or some pronunciation of some silly little detail.
And or but, no it’s got to be but because that typifies — and I’m just sitting here like.

Ho hum hum. And then they give you what they call a storyboard to work from, pictures, like cartoon pictures, and you’ve got to work from that, and you have so much time. Okay you see the film and you time everything up, and make it come out to 30 seconds or whatever it’s going to be. They used to have minute commercials at the time. Then 30 seconds, and then taking ten second from those. And so I’d have to time everything out and get my stopwatch and I’d be sitting there working it out, adjust the tempo a little bit, yeah, a little faster, okay, boom, it came out right at the end you know.
He was very good at it you know.
So I submitted a lot of things. We finally did Cheerios. We did Plymouth Automobiles, we did Borden’s Instant Coffee.
We did a car thing for Plymouth Automobile with Red Norvo actually, he was on the thing.

And a lot of these major accounts we got into, and we made a fortune doing it. Singing, of course I got the fee for arranging, I got the creative fee, I got the fee for leader, I got the fee for piano.
Take those “fi’s” right to the bank.
And then I got very — I listened and I said wait a minute, there’s an announcer’s job comes out of this too. So at the end I would say, we’d finish the music, everything is

done, I’d say why don’t you have me just read the copy so the announcer knows where it goes in this particular piece of music, so he knows when to come in, when to go out. “Good idea, that’ll help us a lot.” And so I’d give it “Cheerios,” I’d give it like a big smile and like read that stuff.
And he knew right where to put it because he’s a musician.

When to get out, when to finish, when to come in. And usually it took about three days, and they would call up and say, “would you be interested in doing the voiceover.” And I’d say, “oh sure, that’d be wonderful.” So — I loved it.
Yeah it was great. Well it helped us to buy our house that we have now.
